points.reason: The registered state, lock state and request-pending state determine arbitration and can be corrupted to select or indefinitely retain the wrong requester.
The combinational select and next-state logic chooses the requester and request strobe, so corruption can misroute or suppress service.
The select chooses which request reaches the shared output and stb can block the transaction.
sel gates acknowledgement and error responses, allowing a response to be delivered to or withheld from requester A.
sel gates acknowledgement and error responses, allowing a response to be delivered to or withheld from requester B.
The decoded selection bits choose enabled address regions and the fallback target, so corruption can select the wrong target or no intended target.
port_sel controls each target request strobe and can redirect or suppress the routed transaction.
The selected-route bit becomes halt and can suppress timeout completion, allowing a selected transfer to remain blocked or fault incorrectly.
The monitor stores and increments the timeout counter and generates keeper.err, so corruption can falsely fault, accept, stall or prematurely terminate a transaction.
The response acknowledgement controls whether the monitor terminates before timeout, so altering the combined response can suppress or induce timeout behavior.
keeper.err directly changes response acknowledgement and error signaling, which can falsely complete or block the bus operation.
keeper.halt is sampled from the selected route and directly suppresses timeout error generation, allowing a stalled transfer to remain blocked.
The selected-route value determines whether keeper.halt is asserted and therefore whether timeout protection is suppressed.
The inline address comparison directly gates each device request strobe, so altering the comparison inputs or gating can select the wrong device or suppress every request.
The child instance supplies the address and strobe used by the inline device comparison; its registered or forwarded values can therefore alter or withhold device selection.
The registered arbiter state stores the atomic-operation phase and can be forced to skip, repeat or hold a phase.
The next-state logic defines read, execute, write and wait transitions, so corruption can reorder phases or prevent completion.
The state selects write data and controls the system request strobe and direction, allowing the atomic access to be changed or blocked.
The state controls response data, acknowledgement and error release, so a corrupted phase can return an invalid result or withhold completion.
The request operand and prior system data enter the captured update-value path and can be observed or altered before storage.
The arbiter registers store the operands used to compute the update, and clock or reset interference can prevent the value from being retained.
The comparison operand contains captured prior data and contributes to the selected atomic update value.
The comparison operand contains captured write data and contributes to the selected atomic update value.
The comparison result decides which operand becomes the update value, so corruption changes the atomic result.
It computes the comparison-based atomic update candidate from captured operands.
The clocked ALU computes and stores the final update value, so it is directly observable or alterable and can fail to produce it.
The computed update value crosses the unit on sys_req_o.data and its release is gated by the atomic state.
The system response data is captured as the prior-value result and can be changed before storage.
arbiter.rdata stores the prior value returned to the core, and clock or reset interference can erase or prevent that result.
The captured prior value is present in the comparison path and can influence the computed atomic update.
The comparison decision can alter the computed update derived from the prior value.
It computes a value from the captured prior operand that feeds the ALU.
The ALU uses the prior value to compute and store the update, so corruption changes the result and failure to produce it can block the operation.
The stored prior value is returned in core_rsp_o.data and the state controls whether the core receives a completed response.
The prior value contributes to the update value sent to sys_req_o.data, exposing its influence outside the unit.
The registered state records reservation progress and controls whether a conditional store is forwarded or completed.
The AMO classification controls reservation-state transitions and can cause an invalid store to be treated as conditional or suppress a valid one.
The reservation state gates the system request strobe for conditional stores, allowing the store to be wrongly issued or withheld.
The gated request strobe crossing the system boundary determines whether the conditional store is performed.
sc_fail records the conditional-store result from the request classification and reservation state, so corruption can report a false failure or success.
sc_fail changes the response acknowledgement and data result, allowing the core to receive an incorrect result or no valid completion.
